claims: the test exercises the real approval path end to end (built CLI, chat-completions mock provider over HTTP, non-interactive auto-approval policy, real shell side effects)

it catches the original approval-reuse bug: same-id cases fail when the per-call approval lookup is reverted, missing-id cases fail when the adapter id fallback is reverted, all four fail with both reverted

it is not a unit test hidden in an integration file: it spawns the compiled CLI in a child process and asserts only filesystem side effects, the child's stderr, and the HTTP requests the provider mock received
no state leaks into the real ~/.term2, ~/.local/state/term2-nodejs or project .term2
uncertain: only the non-interactive --auto-approve answer path is covered; the TUI, control-socket, ACP and gateway approval paths are not exercised by this test
the missing-id cases go through the openai-compatible chat-completions adapter only; the grok chat path shares the adapter but is not run
the test depends on the shell safety classifier keeping `echo > file` GREEN and `rm file` RED; a classifier change could make it fail for unrelated reasons (it would fail loudly, not pass vacuously)

with a repeated call id, non-interactive stderr omits the `[tool] shell: <command>` line for the later call (the id-less runs show it); cause: SessionToolTracker.dedupeToolStarted (source/services/session/session-tool-tracker.ts:254-270) drops tool_started events whose callId was already seen, so it is display only and does not affect approval
